newsitem.title: USA: GM reports Q2 earnings gain despite strikes.
newsitem.headline: GM reports Q2 earnings gain despite strikes.

text.p: General Motors Corp. Wednesday said earnings rose 11 percent in the second quarter as one-time gains helped offset losses of nearly half a billion dollars from two assembly plant strikes.

The world's largest automaker said it earned $2.1 billion, or $2.68 a share, in the quarter, up from $1.9 billion, or $2.63 a share, a year earlier. The per share results for the latest quarter were a record for GM largely because of $2 billion in stock repurchases the company has made this year.

GM said prolonged strikes at its Oklahoma City car plant and its Pontiac, Mich., truck plant reduced net income by $490 million in the quarter. It lost production of 96,000 vehicles during the strikes.
But the results beat expectations on Wall Street.

Excluding $421 million in gains related to Hughes Electronics Corp. and the sale of GM's interest in Avis Europe, the automaker earned about $1.7 billion, or $2.21 a share, above forecasts of $2.10 a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
GM stock rose as high as $56 before closing at $54.375, up 12.5 cents, in consolidated New York Stock Exchange trading.

"GM's results on both a reported and adjusted basis are a further indication of our operating and financial strength," GM Chairman Jack Smith said in a statement. "It's significant that, even though strike-related losses hit the bottom line pretty hard in the second quarter, we still earned a substantial amount of money during the period."

GM also generated substantial amounts of cash in the quarter, raising its cash on hand at quarter's end to $14.9 billion from $14.6 billion at March 31 despite the strikes and $469 million in stock repurchases during the quarter.
GM's North American operations bore the brunt of the strikes, which contributed to a sharp drop in earnings to $474 million from $705 million in the 1996 period.
Earnings at GM's Delphi Automotive Systems parts unit fell to $310 million from $355 million a year earlier.

GM's International operations earned $488 million during the quqarter, including a $103 million gain from Avis, up from $424 million a year earlier. Earnings in Europe fell to $209 million from $319 million a year earlier.
